sections.text: Introduction

This document outlines the testing procedure P1, to be performed on an annually 
bases as indicated by Y1 in the title block.

The relay 51 GN with type IAC produce generator earth fault protection, and this 
achieved by mounted it on the neutral phase. This procedure details the steps 
required to completely check the proper operation and calibration of the relay 
using secondary injection test set.

The document is formatted the way to minimize the possibility of error 
causing personal injury or damage to equipment.

The first draft initiated by eng. Eslam Mahmoud Abas, tested by eng. Tamer 
Mohamed Mokhtar, accepted by eng. Sawsan Mohamed El-Lethy: Port 
Said general director, approved by eng Mohamed Hesain Ahmed Gomaa: head sector, and certified by eng. Zakaria El-Shahat: EDEPC MPIS 
Coordinator.
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued.

The qualified maintenance staff 
 should carry the suitable ID safety category.
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required.
Equipment isolation (disconnect switches are opened and tagged).

Measure the current circuit of the relay by clip ammeter to be sure that is no 
 current.

Make sure CT secondary are shorted before isolating relay current 
 circuits for test current injection.

Preparation

items: Review the manual and drawings.

Prepare the previous

Check the wires of 
 the relay by hand

Check the AC source 
 is available to the tester

Check the existence 
 of the DC sources in panels

Obtain the input 
 terminals of the relay (current terminals) and also the output terminals

Remove the relay 
 plug and insert the test plug

Disconnect the trip 
 leads of the relay and connect one of them to the timer of the tester

Prepare the test 
 sheet for the tested relay

sections.text:
Testing the 
over current element
Current Setting Test

Connect test between the 
current terminals on the relay (5&6) and the current terminals on the test set

Slowly increase the 
current until the relay pick up and record it as a pick up value

Record this value on the 
test sheet (adjust it if needed)

Increase the injected 
current to a value 25% greater than the operate value

Record this value on the 
test sheet (adjust it if needed)

sections.text: Time setting test

Inject current into relay 
until the relay picks up. Keep this value and switch off the test set.

Connect the relay time 
delayed output contacts (1.2) to the timer contacts of the test set.

Switch on the test set and 
inject current. The timer will stop once the relay has picked up.

Record this value on the 
test sheet (adjust it if needed).

Repeat steps (1.2.3.4) on 
a various pick up values and record these values on the test sheet.

Remove the leads from the 
time delayed contact and the test set.

sections.text:
Circuit 
breaker trip test

Set up the circuit breaker 
for a trip test.

Inject current into the 
relay until the circuit breaker trips at the time delayed setting.

Close the circuit breaker 
again.

Remove the wire from the 
relay time delayed contact terminals No. 2 or 1.

Inject a value of current 
greater than the instantaneous setting suddenly into relay until the circuit 
breaker trips at the instantaneous setting.

Return relay to
service

Disconnect the test leads 
from terminal on the relay.

Remove the test plug from 
the relay.

Put the plug of connection 
for current relay.

Re-install the wire which 
was removed.

Remove the shorts from the 
CT secondary circuits.

Return the relay and power 
equipment to service.

associated with the relay has been isolated, it should be returned to service by 
the following restoration steps:
